newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani province governor resigns with threat.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani province governor resigns with threat.

text.p: The governor of Pakistan's most populous Punjab province, Ahmad Tariq Rahim, resigned on Monday, threatening to make disclosures about critics of his conduct during his four months in office.

In a letter to President Farooq Leghari, whose copies were distributed in the provincial capital Lahore, Rahim said he was resigning because Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party had found it difficult to have a working relationship with him as governor.
"This is surprising in view of the fact that the PML leadership articulated no such qualms during the interim period of the caretaker regime," he said.
He was referring to a caretaker government Leghari had set up to oversee elections after he sacked prime minister Benazir Bhutto on November 5 on disputed charges of misrule.

Rahim, a former member of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party and named governor on November 5 as part of the interim setup, has been accused by the PML of having tried unsucessfully to debar some party leaders from elections.
In his letter, Rahim denied what he called motives attributed to some of his actions and said the oath of his office had precluded him from commenting upon or revealing certain facts.

"But there may be time or occasion in the future when I might have to consider sifting information from fact in order to expose the motives of some of those who have proclaimed to be the self-styled champions of free elections, fairplay and democracy," he said.
Bhutto accuses the caretaker government of rigging the February 3 elections, in which she suffered a crushing defeat. The government denies the charge.
